Pure, no imports. components/ai/splParserCheck.ts vetAdHocQuery(query, { user, signal }): analyzeAdHocSpl, then a POST to /en-US/splunkd/__raw/servicesNS/<user>/splunk_app_sap_logserv/search/parser (parse_only=1, expand_macros=1, output_mode=json, Splunk Web’s CSRF header, the cookie session), then checkParserAgreement. Fails closed: HTTP 400 is parser_rejected; any other non-2xx status, a body that is not JSON, a thrown call, a timeout (PARSER_TIMEOUT_MS, 15 s) or an aborted turn is parser_unavailable. buildParserRequest and interpretParserReply are pure, for the suite. utils/fieldClassification.ts FIELD_CLASSES: every field name the App defines (props / transforms / collections / lookups), one class each — identifier, address, host (hostname opt-in), free_text, safe — plus SPLUNK_FIELD_CLASSES (info_sid, identity, …). isClassifiedIdentifier is OR’d into isIdentifierColumnName, so the table only adds to the name patterns. fieldClassification.consistency-test.ts parses the conf files and fails the build on any App field without a class, or classified weaker than the patterns. Pure. utils/vendorErrorText.ts What the vendor is told about a failed or refused tool call. vendorToolErrorText(detected) returns one of a fixed set of strings built from the HTTP status (an integer 100–599, else omitted) and a class from VENDOR_ERROR_CLASSES (classifyToolError); vendorRefusalText(reason) passes an App-written refusal reason on behind REFUSAL_PREFIX. No imports, so the build gate loads it. utils/savedSearchAllowList.ts The saved-search allow-list built from the intent map (buildAllowedSavedSearches, which returns a frozen, read-only copy with no add, delete or clear), checkSavedSearchName, vetToolCall (refuses an undeclared tool or a saved search outside the catalog, and returns the audit operator / spl), and pickSavedSearchTimeRange / buildSavedSearchArgs (the explicit MCP arguments: name, app = splunk_app_sap_logserv, time range). utils/jailbreakPatterns.ts User-prompt jailbreak-pattern detection. FNV-1a hash + matched-groups + char-class fingerprint capture. utils/vendorColumnText.ts What the vendor is told about a Tier 2 result’s columns: vendorColumnLines(rows, opts) writes every Tier 2 line after Returned N rows in M ms. — the _time range, the withheld-names note and one line per column — buildAuthorContext(texts) reads the call’s author text (the words and quoted AS aliases that make a name sendable, and a pipeline reading of each text), and traceColumn / columnValueRule decide what a column’s values may disclose. Pure (imports piiRedaction.ts and fieldClassification.ts); covered by vendorColumnText.consistency-test.ts. Exports KNOWN_COMMANDS and readerCommandNames for the guard’s suite. utils/piiRedaction.ts Tier 2 PII redaction. Name patterns (isPiiColumn) anchored at the start of the name or after _, ., :, - or a space. The tag is redactionTag(value, key): the first 7 hex digits of HMAC-SHA-256(key, UTF-8 value), synchronous, from @noble/hashes 1.4.0 (crypto.subtle is asynchronous and missing on plain-HTTP Splunk Web). The key is the conversation’s, not the hook instance’s: chatTagKey(conversationId) (the provider’s sessionId) returns one 32-byte key per conversation (newTagKey, crypto.getRandomValues) from a module-level map, so a chat panel closed and reopened on a conversation in progress keeps it, and rotateChatTagKey makes a new one when both the chat and the vendor history are empty (Clear chat); the hook passes it as piiOpts.tagKey (a getter); without a key of at least 16 bytes the module’s own random key is used — there is no unkeyed path. redactFreeTextPii(text, key) (Data Doctor raw samples) takes one key per report. utils/rateLimit.ts Per-user rolling-1-hour rate limit. Records rate_limited_prompt audit event on hit. utils/dailySpend.ts Cumulative-cost daily spend cap. Records daily_spend_cap_hit on overflow. utils/vendorCost.ts Per-vendor pricing table for USD cost estimate, exact-id keyed (an unlisted id costs 0). The Claude 5.x ids carry Anthropic’s first-party rates: input, output, each model’s own cache-read rate, and cache writes at 1.25x input; claude-haiku-5-5 at its rate for prompts up to 100K tokens (the higher tier is not modelled). Bedrock prices are partner-set and never derived from these. vendorCost.consistency-test.ts pins every statically listed model id as priced. utils/drilldownUrls.ts Drill-down and panel-action URL builders (dashboard / Host Details / Splunk Search / Open-in-Search / Job Inspector / results export), plus openInNewTab (centralises the noopener,noreferrer flags), splQuote, and sourcetypeToDashboardSlug. buildFlags.ts Build-time values baked in by webpack DefinePlugin: the TEMPLATES_ONLY feature flag plus the app.conf-derived version / build / build-date values rendered in the About dialog. utils/aiConfigApi.ts Read / write AI Assistant config. PRIMARY store is the KV Store collection logserv_ai_assistant_settings (single row defaults); default/ai_assistant_settings.conf is the fresh-install fallback + one-shot migration source. Resolution order: KV Store → conf → defaults. utils/passwordsApi.ts Read / write credentials from Splunk’s encrypted password store via services/storage/passwords. utils/telemetryConfApi.ts Legal-acknowledgement opt-in tracking. Operator-managed optInVersion is read from default/ai_assistant_acks.conf; user acknowledgement state is written to the KV Store collection logserv_ai_assistant_acks (one row per stanza). state/dashboardRefreshPersistence.ts KV Store CRUD for the per-dashboard auto-refresh picker. default/data/mcp/logserv_intent_map.json The predefined-prompt catalog. default/savedsearches.conf The saved searches that intent-map prompts dispatch. default/ai_assistant_settings.conf Org-wide AI Assistant config defaults. default/ai_assistant_acks.conf Splunk-pattern legal-acknowledgement opt-in version + acknowledgement timestamps.

docs.title: The Hidden<T> / Visible<T> Brand Type Pattern
docs.text:
The privacy invariant — “no raw event and no unsummarized tool result is ever transmitted to any AI vendor; only the active tier’s summary is” — is mechanically enforced via TypeScript brand types split across components/ai/types/Hidden.ts and components/ai/types/Visible.ts:

// components/ai/types/Hidden.ts
declare const HIDDEN_BRAND: unique symbol;
export type Hidden<T> = T & { readonly [HIDDEN_BRAND]: true };
export const markHidden = <T>(v: T): Hidden<T> => v as Hidden<T>;
export const unwrapHidden = <T>(v: Hidden<T>): T => v;

// components/ai/types/Visible.ts
declare const VISIBLE_BRAND: unique symbol;
export type Visible<T> = T & { readonly [VISIBLE_BRAND]: true };
export const markVisible = <T>(v: T): Visible<T> => v as Visible<T>;
export const unwrapVisible = <T>(v: Visible<T>): T => v;

export const sanitize = <T>(
    hidden: Hidden<T>,
    summarizer: (value: T) => string,
): Visible<string> => {
    const inner = unwrapHidden(hidden);
    const summary = summarizer(inner);
    return markVisible(summary);
};

Invariant: the only way to obtain a Visible<string> from a Hidden<T> is via sanitize(hidden, summarizer), whose return type is locked to string so a summarizer cannot pass the result object through. The compiler refuses any other coercion path. The summarizer receives the unwrapped data and returns a summary string; the orchestrator’s call site picks the summarizer based on the active privacy tier (tier1Summary for Tier 1, tier2Summary for Tier 2). The type system cannot see what text the summarizer copies into that string, so the summarizers themselves are the place to audit: tier1Summary writes two numbers, and tier2Summary writes aggregates under the rules of utils/vendorColumnText.ts (below).

Where the chokepoint runs: useAIAssistant.ts sendUserMessage → tool dispatch → MCPClient returns Hidden<MCPToolResult> → sanitize(toolResult, tier === 2 ? tier2Summary : tier1Summary) → resulting Visible<string> is appended to the outbound vendor message buffer.

Where the type system enforces: every outbound vendor message is built from Visible<Message>[]. Anywhere code constructs an outbound message, the types refuse a Hidden<T> value. There is no as any cast; bypassing requires modifying the brand-type code itself, which is reviewed.

Failed calls and refusals — no Splunk or MCP text, in any tier. A type cannot tell error text from data, so the summarizers do not pass it on. When detectToolError(inner) finds an error in a result, tier1Summary and tier2Summary both return wrapAsToolResultData(vendorToolErrorText(detected)) — Tool error (HTTP <status>, class=<class>): <fixed hint> The error text is shown to the user only., with HTTP <status>, left out when the status is not an integer from 100 to 599. The class is one of parse_error, unknown_command, missing_lookup, missing_saved_search, permission, timeout, rate_limited, not_found, server_error, other: fixed regexes over the first 2,000 characters of the message pick it, first match wins, and the status decides when none matches (401/403 permission, 404/410 not_found, 408/504 timeout, 429 rate_limited, 5xx server_error, else other). The message only selects which fixed string is returned; no part of it is sent. Up to build 375 both summaries sent Tool error (HTTP n): plus up to 200 characters of the message, and a Splunk error repeats the failed search, into which a subsearch can put event text. The full message stays in the Hidden result, so ToolResultPanel still shows it to the user; the audit events never carried it.

The three refusals the hook makes before dispatch — the session tool-call cap, vetToolCall (saved search outside the catalog, undeclared tool) and vetAdHocQuery (the SPL guard: the denylist, the allow-list and the search-parser check) — build their vendor summary at the refusal site: sanitize(syntheticHidden, () => wrapAsToolResultData(vendorRefusalText(reason))), with the reason the hook just wrote (capReason, toolVerdict.reason, guardReason). vendorRefusalText prefixes Tool call refused by the App before it ran:, turns control characters other than tab, LF and CR into spaces, replaces <TOOL_RESULT_DATA> tags with <filtered>, and caps the reason at 1,000 characters. It is never applied to a server result, so a server message that imitates a refusal is classified like any other error. Numbers still reach the vendor: a count and a timing on every successful call (Tier 1 and 2), the HTTP status and fixed class on a failed one, and the is_error flag where the wire format has one (Anthropic and Bedrock). In Tier 1 the count is found.length, where found = extractRowsForSummary(inner) — the same result rows Tier 2 counts, so an empty results: [] gives Returned 0 rows — and countRows(inner.content) only when found === null (no row shape: the length of the content array, or totalRowCount); up to build 375 it was always countRows(inner.content), which for the Splunk MCP Server’s envelope is the number of content blocks, normally 1. The timing is inner.executionMs, else the time the browser measured. Tier 1 therefore limits bandwidth rather than making leakage zero: a model writing its own queries can make the timing, the failure and its class, and the count depend on event data, so a few bits per call can leak — up to about log2 of the largest count the server can return through the count (the row limit, or the server’s total for totalRowCount). The session tool-call cap (tool_calls_per_session_cap, default 100) limits the calls per chat session; the counter resets when the chat is cleared (the message list becomes empty), and 0 turns the cap off.

Tier 2 — vendorColumnLines. tier2Summary(inner, fallbackMs, topN, piiOpts, onRedaction, authorTexts) computes const found = extractRowsForSummary(inner). extractRowsForSummary tries, in order, structuredContent.results, the JSON of content[0].text (its .results, or the parsed array), a content array and content.rows. It returns null when none is there, and also for a content array that holds an MCP content block (isMcpContentBlock: a type of text, image, audio, resource or resource_link with a text, data, resource or uri key), so reply text is never taken for a row. With found === null Tier 2 sends only Returned a result that is not in row form, in ${ms}ms.; with no rows, Returned 0 rows in ${ms}ms (no events matched the query in the selected time range).; otherwise Returned ${found.length} rows in ${ms}ms. followed by exactly the lines vendorColumnLines(found, { topN, sanitizeValue: sanitizeAggregateValue, piiOpts, onRedaction, author: buildAuthorContext(authorTexts) }) returns. It reads no column name and no _time itself. The dispatcher builds authorTexts, the text the model or the App wrote for the call: [mcpArgs.query] for splunk_run_query ([] when the query is not a string); [SAVED_SEARCH_SPL[name]] for a saved search in the catalog (an own-property check); otherwise CATALOG_SPLS, the SPL of every intent-map prompt. The author text only decides names and how values are traced, and is never echoed. The rules, in utils/vendorColumnText.ts:

  • Author context (buildAuthorContext(texts) → { words, quotedAliases, readings }). Each text, cut at MAX_QUERY_CHARS (20,000), gives words — every match of NAME_WORD_RE ([A-Za-z0-9_]+) in the whole text, quoted parts included — quotedAliases, every double- or single-quoted token that directly follows the word AS (any case), unquoted, and a reading. The reading tokenizes the text (double-quoted and backquoted text as single tokens; a single-quoted token only when it holds no |, bracket, double quote or line break, so a stray apostrophe is one character and cannot hide the pipes after it; words of [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*; single characters), splits it into commands at pipes outside brackets, and reads it command by command (readPipeline → readCommand) into a FieldState: an env of ColumnTraces by name, wildcard patterns, and a default for any other name: a raw field traced to itself, until a command that rebuilds the result (stats, tstats, chart, timechart, top, rare, xyseries, untable, transpose, fieldsummary) replaces it — with nothing, or with the pivot-cell or mixed trace. The first command needs no pipe: a known command name is read as that command, anything else (a macro included) as the implicit search. A text longer than MAX_QUERY_CHARS, more than MAX_TRACE_COMMANDS (256) commands across the text and its subsearches, or a subsearch deeper than MAX_SUBSEARCH_DEPTH (8), or more than MAX_WILDCARD_PATTERNS (12) wildcard definitions in one text (each resolves through the ones before it, 2^k per column), makes every column untraced (opaqueAll). The first command inside appendpipe […] is always read as a command (readPipeline(…, firstIsCommand)), never as the implicit search.
  • Names (planVendorColumns → isSendableColumnName(name, author)). A name is sent when it is in FIXED_COLUMN_NAMES (count, percent, total, Total, NULL, OTHER, column, sum, avg, min, max, dc, values, earliest, latest, first, last, median, mode, stdev, range, rate, field, distinct_count, is_exact, numeric_count, mean), or when isNameShaped(name) — at most MAX_NAME_CHARS (40) characters and FIELD_NAME_RE (^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{0,39}$) or FUNCTION_NAME_RE (one call over a field-name-shaped argument, * or nothing) — and every word of nameWords(name) is in author.words: whole words, exact case — or the name is in author.quotedAliases, at most 40 characters and matches QUOTED_ALIAS_RE (^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*(?: [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)*$: words separated by single spaces), with every word in author.words. Either way sanitizeAggregateValue must return the name unchanged. Any other name becomes col_N (N = 1-based position among the result’s columns that do not start with _), and the summary adds withheldNote(K) (Column names withheld: K. Each such column is shown as col_N, …). Naming does not depend on the redaction setting. So sum(jsmith) (from timechart count by user | stats sum(*)) is col_N unless the author text has the word jsmith, and username is col_N when the author text has only user.
  • Traces (traceColumn(name, author) → ColumnTrace { traced, count, cell, mixed, fields, why }, merged over every reading that outputs the column; a column no reading outputs is untraced, with every word of the author text as its fields). TRACED only through: the field itself (raw, lookup, by / over, top / rare, table / fields); a statistics function (STAT_FUNCTIONS) over one field, nested included (latest(values(user)) → user, or the column named values(user) when one exists), with or without AS; field AS alias; a rename without wildcards (the source name is deleted); eval x=<one bare [A-Za-z_]\w* field or one single-quoted ref>, assignments read left to right as Splunk evaluates them; lookup … OUTPUT f [AS a] (OUTPUTNEW merges with the existing definition) — an output that echoes a match field (lookupField [AS eventField] before OUTPUT) is that event field’s trace; any other output is { traced, fields: [f, …the match fields' fields] }, traced only when every match field is, so a mapping keyed on an identifier is an identifier; CURATED_LOOKUP_OUTPUTS (the category, source and date of the App’s threat-intel lookups) keep baseTrace(f); and counts — COUNT_TRACE, no fields: c and count bare or as a call, count(eval(…)) included, and dc, distinct_count, estdc or estdc_error over ONE traced, unmixed field (over a computed field it is untraced, with that field’s fields); top / rare’s count and percent (or countfield / percentfield; a positional limit, top 10 uri, is skipped like limit=10); fieldsummary’s count, distinct_count, numeric_count and is_exact; transaction’s eventcount, linecount, closed_txn and field_match_sum. UNTRACED, each with a why: any other eval expression (its fields: the words outside double quotes, also split on ., : and -, the contents of single quotes, and what each resolves to, plus the words of its double-quoted literals as they are; a macro in it reads every word of the text); rex (named groups (?<n>), (?P<n>) and (?'n'), mode=sed, offset_field; the words of the pattern join the fields, and a group merges with the earlier definition of its name — rex sets it only where it matches), spath (the words of the path and output join the fields; the output merges with its earlier definition), fieldformat (untraced, merged with the column’s earlier definition), strcat, bin / bucket, convert, iplocation, transaction’s duration, addtotals / addcoltotals; wildcard rename / AS and wildcard aggregations (patterns); a dynamic {x}= eval target; the split cells of chart / timechart / xyseries (cell: true); transpose, untable and fieldsummary (mixed: true); two different definitions of one name (mergeTraces; two counts stay a count); a column an append / appendcols / join / union / multisearch / set / appendpipe subsearch defines (mergeSub: a field passed through by its own name stays traced; search / where subsearches are not read and add nothing); a field read where it no longer exists (sourceOf). opaqueAll — every column untraced, its fields every word of the text — for lookup without OUTPUT, inputlookup after the first command, foreach, map, any unknown command, a macro as a piped command, and an eval, rename, stats, chart, top, … the reader cannot split. An untraced definition that lists more than MAX_SOURCE_STEPS (64) fields lists every word of the text instead. Every limit fails closed. (This reader replaced round 7’s name graph — sourceFieldNames, hasIdentifierSource, isCountColumn, COUNT_EXPR_RE and the author context’s sources / pivotSources / mixed — which are gone.)
  • Value rule (columnValueRule(name, author, piiOpts) → { trace, identifier, textSafe, numericIdentifier }). identifier is true when isIdentifierColumnName holds for the column’s own name or any of trace.fields — the class table of fieldClassification.ts (identifier and address; host when hostnames are redacted), the piiRedaction name patterns (hostnames when they are redacted) plus id, uid, gid, guid, uuid, pid, ssn, iban, phone, msisdn, imsi, imei, acct and account / card / employee / personnel numbers, as the whole name or after _ . : -, case-insensitive, and camelCase …Id / …ID. textSafe is traced && !count && !cell && !mixed && !identifier; numericIdentifier is !count && (identifier || mixed).
  • Columns past the first 30 are reported only as R more columns not summarized..
  • Numeric values (numericDisclosure(named, columnValueRule(…).numericIdentifier, distinct, piiOpts)). With PII redaction on, a numeric identifier column sends values withheld at any cardinality (withheld-identifier); a column with one distinct value that is not named or is a numeric identifier sends values withheld at any redaction setting; any other numeric column sends min / max / avg / sum, untraced ones and columns shown as col_N included.
  • Time (vendorTimeRangeLine). Every non-null _time must parse (parseVendorTime: an epoch in seconds as a number or digit string, 0 to 2100-01-01, or a strict ISO-8601 timestamp with Z / +hh:mm / +hhmm on a real calendar date); the line is then Time range: <ISO UTC> → <ISO UTC> (UTC). built with new Date(ms).toISOString() — no zone from the data is sent — else Time range: not shown (the _time values are not all timestamps).. A parsed range is sent only when timeRangeAllowed(author): _time traced, not a count, cell or mix, every field in TIME_SOURCE_FIELDS (_time, bucket_ts, day_ts); otherwise TIME_NOT_SHOWN_COMPUTED (Time range: not shown (the query computes _time from other fields).).
  • Categorical values: top-N by count, sanitizeAggregateValue, then — with PII redaction on, unless the column is named and textSafe — redactValueIfPII(PII_STAND_IN_COLUMN, …) (user), so every non-empty value that is not <filtered> becomes a <redacted-…> tag; then 40 characters each, within a 160-character line. A named, traced column whose name and source fields mark no identifier keeps its values; with redaction off every column keeps them.
  • onRedaction (the audit’s tier2RedactionsApplied) fires for each value redacted and for each numeric column withheld as withheld-identifier (an identifier field, or mixed values). A withheld name does not fire it.

What this does not close: Tier 2 sends aggregated event values by design. A column shown as col_N or untraced keeps its numeric statistics unless it is a numeric identifier, and a named, traced column whose name and source fields mark no identifier — an event field, a lookup column not keyed on an identifier, eval m=_raw included — is sent, filtered and cut to 40 characters. Counts are not traced to the fields that shaped them, so a count can carry a few bits a query manufactures (stats count by <a computed multivalue> then stats count); documented, not closed. A name made only of words the model wrote is model-authored text and is sent even when it equals a value the model has seen (… as jsmith, or jsmith typed anywhere in its query); the catalog’s words have the same property. Name-based PII redaction is hygiene for ordinary queries, not a content filter.

Augmenting a Visible<T>-branded string: direct concatenation produces a TS error since the brand type can’t widen back automatically. The pattern is unwrapVisible() + new string + markVisible(). The Power Mode primer augmentation uses this pattern.

docs.title: The Build Flag Pattern (TEMPLATES_ONLY and Future Flags)
How the flag disables the LLM path
docs.text:
TEMPLATES_ONLY is baked into the bundle at build time (webpack DefinePlugin) and cannot be changed post-deploy. Rather than duplicating a guard at every consumer, the flag forces the runtime templates_only_mode value on at the config-read chokepoint:

  1. utils/aiConfigApi.ts — the enforcement point. The flag is OR-ed into templates_only_mode inside parseRawContent (the single normalizer for BOTH the KV Store row and the conf stanza) and into DEFAULT_AI_CONFIG (the both-reads-failed fallback), so EVERY read path reports templates_only_mode: true regardless of what is stored. This is what defeats a stored KV row of 0 carried over from a full-LLM install.
  2. hooks/useAIAssistant.ts — ORs the flag into the sendUserMessage guard as prop-chain-independent defense in depth; a dispatch attempt short-circuits with a system notice directing the user to the prompt browser.
  3. state/AIAssistantConfig.ts — forces the pre-load default, so the UI never renders an LLM-enabled state while config is still loading.
  4. bin/build.js — patches the STAGED conf default to true so the artifact is self-describing (cosmetic; the webapp force is the gate).

What the flag does NOT do: the vendor provider modules (AnthropicProvider.ts, OpenAIProvider.ts, AzureOpenAIProvider.ts, BedrockProvider.ts) remain in the bundle, and their endpoint strings remain visible in home.js. Bundle-level stripping was explicitly declined — this is a functional disable, not a code strip. For policy-driven deployments where the LLM code must be physically absent from the artifact, use the frozen v0.0.6 line, which deletes the provider implementations from source instead.

docs.title: Single source of truth
docs.text: buildFlags.ts is the canonical module for compile-time values — it exports each flag as a typed boolean derived from a build-time substitution. Use sites import the flag from buildFlags.ts rather than reading the underlying env var directly. The two build variants of the same build number differ in exactly two bundle regions — the compiled flag module and styled-components’ per-build salt — and that byte-diff is the proof the full-LLM build is otherwise unchanged.

docs.title: The Chat Citation Parser
docs.text:
components/ai/chat/ChatMessage.tsx parses inline markers in assistant_text + guidance messages. The regex:

const TEXT_PATTERN = /\[(?:→|->)\s*([a-zA-Z0-9_:.\-]+)\]|\[severity:(critical|high|medium|low)\]|\*\*([^*]+)\*\*/g;

Three numbered capture groups disambiguate which alternative fired:

Group Pattern Renders as 1 [→ logserv_xxx] or [-> logserv_xxx] Clickable scroll-to-tile span via onJumpToResult(toolUseId); auto-appends sibling ↗ Dashboard chip(s) + ↗ Run SPL chip 2 [severity:critical|high|medium|low] Glossy colored dot via <SeverityDot $level={level} /> 3 **bold text** Bold-stripped: the ** markers are dropped and the inner text is re-parsed recursively for nested citation / severity markers (build 174 fix)

The recursive-parse fix (build 174): when the AI drifts and emits **[severity:medium]** (markdown bold wrapping the severity marker), the bold alternative matches first and would render the inner text as plain string, losing the severity dot. The fix recursively calls renderTextWithCitations() on the bold inner content. Save/restore of TEXT_PATTERN.lastIndex around the recursive call is required because the regex is module-scoped + /g-stateful — not saving would corrupt the outer iteration.

Why module-scoped state: lastIndex reset at function entry handles the common case. For recursive parses, save/restore around the call is required.

Alternatives considered for the bold-wrapped severity marker: re-ordering the regex alternatives so severity matches first doesn’t help — bold wraps around the severity, so even if severity tries first, it can’t match inside an unmatched bold span. Updating the primer to forbid bold around severity markers helps future prompts but doesn’t repair existing UI; the parser must be tolerant either way.

docs.title: The MCP Tool Definitions Sent on Every Free-Form Request
docs.text: The AI sees these two tool definitions on every free-form request. The source of truth is DEFAULT_TOOLS in hooks/useAIAssistant.ts (TypeScript field inputSchema); the definitions are sent as the request’s top-level tools array — the primer separately teaches the AI when to use each. The block below shows the Anthropic wire form (input_schema; the OpenAI/Azure path maps the same schema to function.parameters):

docs.title: splunk_run_saved_search
docs.text:
{
    "name": "splunk_run_saved_search",
    "description": "Dispatch a saved search from the LogServ App's catalog.",
    "input_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
            "name": {"type": "string", "description": "Saved-search name from the catalog (e.g., logserv_hana_failed_auth_24h)"},
            "earliest_time": {"type": "string", "description": "Splunk earliest token (-24h, -7d, etc.)"},
            "latest_time": {"type": "string", "description": "Splunk latest token (now, etc.)"},
            "render_hint": {"type": "string", "enum": ["table", "timechart", "kpi", "pie"]},
            "top_n": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 50, "description": "Width of categorical aggregates the AI receives in Tier 2 summary. Default 10."}
        },
        "required": ["name"]
    }
}

The schema carries no enum of names: the catalog reaches the AI as primer text, and the name is checked at run time.

How a saved-search call is dispatched. Every splunk_run_saved_search call — a predefined prompt from the prompt browser and a free-form tool call alike — goes through MCPClient.runSavedSearch, the single choke point:

  • Allow-list. The allowed names are the saved-search names in logserv_intent_map.json (the 48 read-only prompts and the 13 ES correlation searches); useAIAssistant.ts builds the set from the intent map it already imports, so the allow-list, the primer catalog and the prompt browser cannot drift apart. The match is exact and case-sensitive. buildAllowedSavedSearches returns a frozen ReadonlySet<string> view over a private copy of the names: it has no add, delete or clear (a cast does not help — they are not functions), Set.prototype.add.call on it throws, and its members cannot be replaced, so no code that holds the list can widen it. Every rollup aggregation, retention, backfill and ES feed is outside it, so the AI cannot run one.
  • Explicit arguments. buildSavedSearchArgs builds the MCP arguments field by field from the vetted name (saved_search_name), the App (app = splunk_app_sap_logserv, so the server runs this App’s search and not a same-named one elsewhere) and the time range (earliest_time / latest_time); the model’s arguments object is no longer spread into them, so it cannot replace saved_search_name or add keys.
  • Refusal. A name outside the allow-list is refused before any MCP request. For a free-form tool call, vetToolCall in the tool loop refuses it before the call reaches runSavedSearch: the AI receives a synthetic error tool_result, and a security_blocked_spl audit event records spl = (saved search) <name> with operator = saved_search_not_in_catalog. The choke point itself only returns the isError result; predefined prompts take their names from the intent map, and the allow-list consistency suite checks that every one of them is allowed.
  • Unknown tools. Only the two tools in DISPATCHABLE_TOOLS (the two offered in DEFAULT_TOOLS) are dispatched; vetToolCall refuses any other tool name the model emits instead of forwarding it to the MCP server, with a security_blocked_spl audit event (spl = (tool) <name>, operator = tool_not_declared).

docs.title: splunk_run_query
docs.text: Same schema shape but accepts a query (SPL string) instead of name. Before dispatch the hook awaits vetAdHocQuery(adHocQuery, { user: ctx.user, signal: controller.signal }) (components/ai/splParserCheck.ts; a query that is not a string is checked as the empty query, and refused): the denylist, the allow-list, then Splunk’s search parser. Any refusal is recorded, sent to the vendor as the App’s reason, and the query is never dispatched.

docs.title: The SPL Static-Analysis Guard
docs.text:
utils/splGuard.ts has two fences. The first, analyzeSpl(spl: string): { blocked: boolean; reason?: string; operator?: string }, is a denylist: it refuses a known list of risky commands — Splunk’s own, with every alias Splunk declares for them (checked against system/default/searchbnf.conf of Splunk 9.4.3), and a few named third-party ones — and passes every other command. The second, the allow-list (analyzeAdHocSpl, below), refuses every command, lookup and data source that is not on its lists, so another installed app’s custom commands and external lookups are refused even when the denylist does not name them. The denylist refuses a query at the first of seven checks that fails, in this order:

  1. Inline comment (operator = inline_comment) — three backticks anywhere. Splunk drops a comment before it runs the search, so a comment placed inside a word (saved + comment + search, or between | and outputlookup) would hide that word from the checks below. Any comment is refused rather than stripped.
  2. Unmatched backtick (unbalanced_backtick) — an odd number of backticks, so a macro reference cannot be left open.
  3. Ambiguous quoting — a double quote that is never closed (unterminated_quote), or a backslash-escaped double quote outside a quoted string (escaped_quote). Either would make the guard’s idea of what is quoted differ from Splunk’s. From here on, checks 4 and 6 read the copy that blankQuotedStrings(query) returns: the content of every double-quoted string replaced by spaces, backslash escapes inside a string honoured (\" and \\ do not end it), the quote characters and the length kept. Quoted text then cannot fake a command position ("[DELETE]", "(?<tag>[AI])"). Only double quotes are blanked: a | or [ inside single quotes counts as a command position, which only ever refuses more. Every check that a word split by quotes could dodge also reads a second copy, dequoted: the query with every quote character, double and single, removed and the quoted content kept ("saved"search reads as savedsearch, 'in'to as into). Splunk may or may not join such pieces into one word; the guard assumes it does and fails closed.

  4. Forbidden command or word (operator = the matched name, lower-cased):

    export const FORBIDDEN_SPL_COMMANDS = [
    'collect', 'stash', 'summaryindex', 'sumindex',
    'mcollect', 'meventcollect',
    'outputlookup', 'outputcsv', 'outputtext',
    'delete',
    'sendalert', 'sendemail',
    'script', 'run', 'runshellscript',
    'dump', 'tscollect', 'createrss',
    'rest', 'outputtelemetry',
    'curl', 'wget', 'sendresults',
    'ai', 'deletemodel',
    'macro', 'savedsplunk',
    'map',
] as const;

export const FORBIDDEN_SPL_WORDS = ['savedsearch', 'savedsplunk'] as const;

    (The source lists them one per line, each with a comment and, for Splunk’s own commands, its searchbnf.conf line; map stays last because the build gate reads the list.) A command is matched at command position on the quote-blanked copy; a word anywhere in the raw query, quoted text included, and then anywhere in dequoted (| "saved"search X, | from "saved"search:X). A command word written with double or single quotes in it (| "delete", | de"lete", | de'lete') is refused as well: at each command position of the blanked copy the guard reads the word from the raw query, removes its quote characters, and refuses it when it starts with a forbidden command or a forbidden word (| sav"edsearch" X), reporting that name as the operator. macro is refused at command position only, because it is a common word.

  5. External lookup (external_lookup) — EXTERNAL_LOOKUPS = ['dnslookup'], Splunk’s own external lookup (system/default/transforms.conf, external_cmd = external_lookup.py clienthost clientip). Each row is a DNS query, so a value built into a host name reaches the domain’s name server. Refused as a word anywhere in the raw query or in dequoted: lookup dnslookup ..., a quoted name, a name split by quotes ("dns"lookup), the eval lookup() function. Every other lookup, the App’s included, passes.

  6. MLTK fit ... into (fit_into, fitThenInto) — fit ... into saves or overwrites a model. At each command position of the blanked copy, the command word counts as fit when the blanked text there starts with fit, (fit"a"), or the raw word with its quote characters removed does ("fit", f'it'). From the first such position, the query is refused when the word into appears anywhere up to the END of the query, in that remainder with its quote characters removed ("in"to) or turned into spaces ("a"into). The scan does not stop at the next | or ], because either may sit inside a single-quoted field name ('a|b'), and quoted text counts. fit with no into after it, and apply, only read and stay allowed.
  7. Macro (macro) — every backtick pair must reference one of ALLOWED_SPL_MACROS, the stanza names of the App’s default/macros.conf (sap_logserv_idx_macro, sap_logserv_audit_idx_macro, sap_logserv_cloud_provider_default_macro; the allow-list consistency suite compares the two), exactly: the bare name for a stanza without arguments, or name(a, ...) with as many arguments as a name(n) stanza declares. Whitespace around the name, a case variant, or name() on a stanza without arguments is refused. A macro’s definition is not visible to the guard, and the Splunk MCP Server’s own parser check runs with macros unexpanded, so any other macro could hide any command.

Why each command is listed: collect and its aliases stash, summaryindex and sumindex, mcollect and meventcollect write to an index; outputlookup and outputcsv write lookup files, and outputtext rewrites each result’s _raw into _xml; delete deletes events; sendalert and sendemail trigger alert actions; script, its alias run, and runshellscript run scripts; dump writes search results to files on the search head; tscollect writes tsidx summaries; createrss adds an item to an RSS feed on the search head (the search app’s commands.conf marks it is_risky); rest reads any REST endpoint the user may read, including storage/passwords, whose clear_password is every stored credential, decrypted; outputtelemetry sends rows to Splunk’s telemetry service; the third-party curl and wget (for example from TA-webtools) send HTTP requests to any URL, and sendresults emails results; ai (Machine Learning Toolkit / AI Toolkit) sends the piped rows to the LLM configured there, which would break the App’s rule that no event data reaches an AI vendor; deletemodel deletes a saved model; savedsearch, its aliases macro and savedsplunk, and map run another saved search (or a search per result row), which would reach the rollup, retention and backfill searches the saved-search allow-list keeps out.

Detection (the command, word and external-lookup regexes are all case-insensitive):

  • The command regex, (?:^|\||\[)\s*(<command>)\b, runs on the quote-blanked copy. It fires at the start of the query, after a pipe, or after a subsearch bracket, so | collect index=x, [| outputlookup x] and a query that starts outputlookup x are all caught, while a field value such as action="collect_data", a field named fitness or rest_time, or a bracketed tag inside a quoted string (search "[DELETE]") is not.
  • The word regex, \b(<word>)\b, runs on the raw query and then on dequoted, and fires anywhere, which catches | from savedsearch:X, | union savedsearch:X, [savedsearch X], | from "savedsearch:X" and | "saved"search X. A field such as savedsearch_name is not affected, because of the word boundary. The external-lookup regex works the same way (dnslookup_cache passes).

Known, deliberately conservative false positives: the words savedsearch, savedsplunk and dnslookup inside quoted text (for example index=_audit "savedsearch"), and words that only form once quote characters are removed ("saved""search", x="dns"lookup); a backtick, or three, inside a quoted value; a query that starts with a command word, plain or quoted (delete ..., "run" ..., 'run' ...), which Splunk would read as a search term; a | or [ inside a single-quoted string, read as a command position; a fit followed anywhere later by the word into, even when into belongs to another command or to quoted text (| fit X | stats count by into, | fit X by "a into b", | fit X | eval note="into", or into in a later subsearch); and a backslash-escaped double quote outside a quoted string. Read-only queries with apostrophes ("don't") and single-quoted field names that spell nothing forbidden pass the denylist. A denylist refusal names no other command or macro; with the allow-list behind it there is no perimeter left to map, so allow-list refusals name the refused command or lookup and the primers list the allowed commands exactly. A macro that takes arguments needs a review before it is added to macros.conf: its arguments are substituted into its definition, so one that puts an argument where a command can go would let the arguments carry any command.

docs.title: The allow-list (analyzeAdHocSpl)
docs.text:
analyzeAdHocSpl(query): AdHocSplAnalysis runs the denylist first (a denylist refusal keeps its operator, and command is set when the operator is a forbidden command or word), then:

  1. Data scope on the raw query, double-quoted text blanked (index_not_allowed): an index=, index!=, index==, index:: or index IN ( term (INDEX_TERM_RE, also a double-quoted "index" name); OR or NOT right before, or OR right after, `sap_logserv_idx_macro` (Splunk binds OR tighter than the implied AND). A backtick inside quoted text is macro_position.
  2. The lexer (lexSpl): its problems become ambiguous_single_quote, unbalanced_bracket, escaped_outside_quotes (a backslash outside double quotes) and macro_position (a macro written against other text, the lexer’s macro_adjacent); too_deep is reported as subsearch_not_allowed.
  3. The command tree, every pipeline (checkPipeline, with the mode main, filter for a search subsearch, arm for append / appendcols / join, pipe for appendpipe): every command name in ALLOWED_SPL_COMMANDS (47 commands, each one the Tier 2 reader reads in full; command_not_allowed, also for a command with no name; union is off the list - Splunk’s search parser reported every union rewritten, as search … | append [...] or multisearch, in the live probe P2, so checkParserAgreement would refuse each one - and its refusal carries COMMAND_INSTEAD.union, which tells the model to combine searches with append); every macro where it cannot change the scope — the data macro as the first term of a search or right after WHERE in tstats, the audit macro never (index_not_allowed), an App macro that expands to a command only as that whole command (macro_position); the start of the query and of every subsearch arm (query_start): the data macro as the first term of its search, | inputlookup, | tstats … WHERE <data macro> or | makeresults, and every later tstats too; lookup / inputlookup names in ALLOWED_SPL_LOOKUPS (the App’s transforms.conf lookup stanzas minus EXCLUDED_SPL_LOOKUPS: the two Data Doctor collections and the two ES feeds; lookup_not_allowed) and no eval lookup(, whitespace or a line break before the parenthesis included (eval_lookup); subsearch groups only in SUBSEARCH_HOSTS, one for appendpipe (subsearch_not_allowed); a filter subsearch ending with fields / table naming its fields, none search or query (subsearch_fields).

A refusal carries command: the refused name, through safeName ([A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}, else (unnamed)). A pass carries commands (the top-level command names, macro commands expanded) and startsWithDataMacro.

The search-parser check (checkParserAgreement(local, body), called by vetAdHocQuery): the reply of search/parser (parse only, macros expanded, in the user’s namespace of this App) must have a commands list (readParserReply; a reply without one, or one with more than PARSER_REPLY_MAX_NODES nodes, is parser_unavailable); every command anywhere in it must be allowed (in the replies the live probe P2 recorded only the top-level commands are command nodes: a subsearch is text, macros expanded, inside the raw arguments of the command that holds it); its top-level list must equal commands (PARSER_COMMAND_ALIASES: bucket = bin); when the query starts with the data macro, the first search’s raw arguments must start with the shipped definition, not followed by OR / NOT (dataMacroAsShipped; raw arguments that still hold a backtick are not judged); no top-level command’s raw arguments may name another index (foreignIndexTerm); and (build 378) every top-level lookup / inputlookup must name, in its raw arguments, one of ALLOWED_SPL_LOOKUPS (parserLookupName: the first word after the options PARSER_LOOKUP_OPTIONS documents for that command, each with a plain value; the word must end at whitespace or the end of the text; anything it cannot read - no raw arguments, an option the command does not document or one in another case, a quoted or glued option value or name - refuses too, with command = the command). The raw arguments are the command’s text after its name, macros expanded, as the live parser probe recorded them (logserv_wp_perf_rollup where metric="wperr"); a lookup or command inside a subsearch is no command of its own in the reply, so the lexer alone checks it, and one that a shadowed macro brings into a subsearch is caught by neither check (only an index term it brings in is, through foreignIndexTerm on the raw arguments of the command that holds the subsearch). Any disagreement is parser_mismatch. For a query that starts with the data macro this also catches a macro of the same name that the user’s context shadows; the macro after WHERE in tstats or at the start of a subsearch is checked only through foreignIndexTerm. A parser_mismatch reason quotes at most one command name from the reply, through safeName; no other reply text reaches the vendor.

Limits. Catalog searches are not checked this way: a local/macros.conf override in this App, the user’s private macro or another app’s globally exported macro of the same name can still change what a catalog search reads; keeping the three macros unshadowed is the admin’s responsibility (splunk btool macros list <name> --debug shows the one in effect). The parser check depends on search/parser being reachable; when it is not, every free-form query is refused.

Audit on block: (none when the user stopped the turn while the parser call ran: parser_unavailable with the turn’s signal aborted, stoppedByUser in the hook) security_blocked_spl event with spl (the query, truncated to 1000 chars) + operator (the matched command or word, or inline_comment / unbalanced_backtick / unterminated_quote / escaped_quote / external_lookup / fit_into / macro; macro is reported both for a macro outside the App’s own and for the macro command, and command tells them apart — the macro’s name as written (foreignMacroName), or macro; for the allow-list command_not_allowed, query_start, index_not_allowed, lookup_not_allowed, eval_lookup, subsearch_not_allowed, subsearch_fields, macro_position, ambiguous_single_quote, unbalanced_bracket; for the parser check parser_mismatch, parser_rejected or parser_unavailable) + command when the refusal is about a command, lookup or macro. The Session-audit modal and the Audit Log viewer show it next to the operator. The AI receives Tool call refused by the App before it ran: followed by the guard’s reason (see Failed calls and refusals above), and can recover by writing a different query.

Scope: only AI-authored splunk_run_query SPL. Pre-authored saved searches dispatched via splunk_run_saved_search are NOT subject to the guard — their SPL is reviewed at build time, and only the intent map’s names can be dispatched (see How a saved-search call is dispatched above).

docs.title: Audit Event Schemas
docs.text:
All audit events extend the AuditEventBase shape:

interface AuditEventBase {
    category: AuditCategory; // discriminator — the string-literal union
                             // that must be extended when adding a category
    timestamp: string;       // ISO-8601 UTC
    user: string;            // Splunk username
    sessionId: string;       // Per-tab session UUID
    seq: number;             // Monotonic per-session sequence
}

Per-category extras:

Category Extra fields local_only (LocalOnlyEvent) promptId: string, spl: string, rowCount: number, executionMs: number, ok: boolean vendor_tier1 (VendorTier1Event — one per completed free-form prompt, at any tier; it does not carry the tier) provider, model, inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedInputTokens?, cacheCreationInputTokens?, vendorCostEstimateUsd, outboundBytes, outboundSha256, promptLength, toolDefCount, turnCount, tier2RedactionsApplied?: number (the onRedaction count; 0 in Tier 1), powerMode?: boolean vendor_tier2 (VendorTier2Event — declared but never emitted; every vendor call records vendor_tier1) provider, model, outboundBytes, outboundSha256, aggregateKind, userApproved, distinctValueCount vendor_tier2_elevation previousTier, newTier security_blocked_spl (SecurityBlockedSplEvent) spl (truncated to 1000 chars), operator: string, command?: string. Emitted for a blocked splunk_run_query (spl = the query; operator = the forbidden command or word, or inline_comment / unbalanced_backtick / unterminated_quote / escaped_quote / external_lookup / fit_into / macro, an allow-list operator or a parser-check operator — see the SPL guard above; command = the refused command, lookup or macro), for a refused saved-search name (spl = (saved search) <name>, operator = saved_search_not_in_catalog) and for an undeclared tool (spl = (tool) <name>, operator = tool_not_declared) rate_limited_prompt (RateLimitedPromptEvent) threshold, countInWindow, promptLength, secondsUntilNextSlot user_prompt_jailbreak_flag (UserPromptJailbreakFlagEvent) promptHash (FNV-1a 32-bit hex), promptLength, matchedGroups: string[], charClassFingerprint: string session_tool_cap_hit (SessionToolCapHitEvent) cap, attemptedCount, toolName daily_spend_cap_hit (DailySpendCapHitEvent) capUsd, spentTodayUsd, promptLength, secondsUntilMidnight audit_forwarder_failure destinationUrl (sanitized — query strings stripped), reason, batchSize forwarder_disabled_acceptance / ai_assistant_enable_acceptance host (Splunk-stamped IP), tcVersion, optInChoice, disclaimerHash model_discovery (ModelDiscoveryEvent) provider, trigger (credential_save / settings_refresh / ttl), ok, modelCount, durationMs, error

All schemas live at components/ai/audit/auditTypes.ts.

docs.title: Splunk reserved-field gotcha
docs.text: The category field on these events is a Splunk reserved name. The viewer’s SPL uses | eval category=json_extract(_raw, "category") after spath because spath does NOT overwrite reserved fields. Replicate this pattern in custom queries.

docs.title: Adding a New Predefined Prompt
docs.text:
1. Edit default/data/mcp/logserv_intent_map.json — add a new entry to the prompts array. Required fields: id, pack (sap_basis | security | operations — drives which prompt-browser tab the prompt appears under), savedSearch, label, description, spl, renderHint. Type-optional but present on every shipped prompt (omitting them silently degrades the guidance card, the deep-dive links, and the Dashboard-Focused tab): interpretation, nextSteps, dashboard. Truly optional: chartHint, chartPalette.
  2. Edit default/savedsearches.conf — add a stanza with the same name as the prompt’s savedSearch field. The SPL must match byte-for-byte.
  3. Bump the intent map’s top-level version field.
  4. Run yarn check:intent-map — it also runs automatically as the FIRST step of yarn build / yarn build:templates-only, so drift fails in seconds, before webpack. It asserts byte-equality between each prompt’s spl and its savedsearches.conf stanza, and that every prompt-shaped stanza has a prompt (scheduled rollup jobs are exempt). The sibling gate yarn check:diagnostics runs the other consistency-test suites plus live conf-drift checks and must also pass for any build.
  5. Pre-deploy SPL dry-run. Dispatch the new prompt’s SPL via services/search/jobs/oneshot against live data: 
    curl -sk -u admin:<pw> --data-urlencode "search=<your spl>" \
    -d output_mode=json -d earliest_time=-30d -d latest_time=now \
    https://localhost:8089/services/search/jobs/oneshot
    Confirm the result has rows with the expected fields. ~50% of new prompts fail static review with field-extraction issues that only surface against live data.
  6. Bump UI App [install] build in app.conf to bust Splunk Web’s static-asset cache.

docs.title: Intent map JSON schema
docs.text:
interface IntentMapPrompt {
    id: string;
    pack: 'sap_basis' | 'security' | 'operations';
    savedSearch: string;
    label: string;
    description: string;
    spl: string;
    renderHint: 'table' | 'timechart' | 'kpi' | 'pie';
    chartHint?: 'timechart' | 'kpi' | 'pie';
    chartPalette?: 'volume' | 'errors' | 'errors-2' | 'errors-3' | 'auth' | 'status' | 'categorical' | 'neutral';
    dashboard?: string | string[];
    interpretation?: string;
    nextSteps?: Array<string | { text: string; savedSearch?: string; spl?: string }>;
}

docs.title: Splunk risky-command safeguard
docs.text:
Splunk Web’s Search app has a safety modal on these commands: map, runshell, script, delete, crawl, tscollect, loadjob, outputlookup, outputcsv, sendalert, sendemail. URLs to /app/search/search?q=... containing one of these triggers the modal.

Scan all SPL — including nextSteps.spl deep-dive strings — for risky commands before shipping. Rewrite map-style cross-row dispatches to first-class subsearch syntax: [ search ... | top 1 X | fields X ].

docs.title: Adding a New Audit Event Category
docs.text:
1. Edit components/ai/audit/auditTypes.ts — add a new TypeScript interface extending AuditEventBase with the category-specific fields. Add the type to the AuditEvent union.
  2. Add the new category id to the discriminator string-literal type.
  3. Find the call site that should emit the event. Construct the event object and call ctx.actions.recordAudit(event).
  4. Edit utils/auditQuery.ts — add the category id to AUDIT_CATEGORIES (keep it alphabetical; this drives the viewer’s filter chips and the category union).
  5. Edit components/AuditLogViewer.tsx — add a case to renderHighlight so the row shows its most actionable fields. Do NOT append to CATEGORY_ACCENT_ORDER unless ACCENT_PALETTE grows in lockstep — it maps positionally onto the 11-colour palette; an unlisted category deliberately falls back to the dormant grey via chipColorForCategory.
  6. Bump the UI App build.

The audit writer (components/ai/audit/auditWriter.ts) sends events to BOTH the local logserv_ai_assistant_audit index AND the optional HEC forwarder. No code change needed at the writer layer for new categories.

docs.title: System Primer Architecture
docs.text:
Two primer variants ship: SYSTEM_PRIMER_TIER1 and SYSTEM_PRIMER_TIER2. Both live in hooks/useAIAssistant.ts as module-private constants (only SAVED_SEARCH_DASHBOARDS and the hook itself are exported — a consumer needing primer text must export it first). They share most of their content; the differences:

  • Tier 1 primer instructs the AI that summaries it receives are count + execution-time only, and to write SHAPE-aware narrative (“X rows returned for the search’s rolling window”) rather than inventing concrete values.
  • Tier 2 primer informs the AI that summaries include aggregated metadata (per-column cardinality, top-N values + counts, numeric stats, time range), and instructs it to ground every claim in the actual values from the aggregates. Its TIER 2 SUMMARY SHAPES block explains col_N and the withheld-names line, <redacted-…> tags, values withheld, not in row form and Time range: not shown, and tells the model never to guess, recover or attribute a withheld name or a redacted value and to name an identifier only when it appears in clear; synthesis rule 3 grounds claims in values shown in clear.

Both primers include:

  • The TOOL_RESULT_DATA boundary block (<TOOL_RESULT_DATA>...</TOOL_RESULT_DATA> sentinels)
  • The TIME-WINDOW REASONING block (build 171)
  • The canonical saved-search catalog
  • The LogServ data model (sourcetypes + key fields, for ad-hoc SPL)
  • The decision rule for splunk_run_saved_search vs splunk_run_query
  • The SYNTHESIS RULES section: lettered finding format, severity-dot rendering, citation format, etc.

Power Mode augmentation: when the user has Power Mode on, POWER_MODE_RULE_SUFFIX is appended to the primer at dispatch time via unwrapVisible(content) + suffix then markVisible() (the brand type can’t widen back automatically).

docs.title: Pre-Resolving Drill-Down URLs at the Orchestrator Layer
docs.text:
The drill-down chip URLs (↗ Dashboard, ↗ Run SPL) are pre-resolved at the AIAssistant.tsx layer, where each tool result’s exact dispatch window is known. The resolved URLs are stored on the citationLookup Map for the chat parser to consume:

const citationLookup: Map<string, { toolUseId: string; splUrl?: string }> = new Map();
toolResultsInOrder.forEach((tr) => {
    if (tr.displayName) {
        const splUrl = tr.spl
            ? buildSplunkSearchUrl(tr.spl, tr.earliest, tr.latest)
            : undefined;
        citationLookup.set(tr.displayName, { toolUseId: tr.toolUseId, splUrl });
    }
});

The chat-side renderer (ChatMessage.tsx) is dumb — it just renders <a href={entry.splUrl}> when the lookup carries a URL. This avoids duplicating SPL-lookup logic at every consumer.

Same pattern applies to the dashboard chips (build 156): the dashboardLinks are resolved once via resolveDashboardLinks(slugs) at the orchestrator and consumed as {slug, name, url} triples.

docs.title: Legal Acknowledgement Modal Trigger Logic
docs.text:
Two legal acknowledgement modals gate Settings save flows:

  • Enable Acceptance Modal — gates enabled = true saves.
  • Forwarder Disabled Acceptance Modal — gates audit_forwarder_enabled = false saves.

Both follow Splunk’s splunk_instrumentation optInVersion framework with one extension. The trigger logic is:

isEnableTcPending = (
    (saved.enabled === false && draft.enabled === true)  // deliberate toggle-on
    OR
    (currentOptInVersion > acknowledgedVersion)          // version bumped
)

The pure optInVersion-only path is what Splunk’s stock telemetry uses (acknowledge once per version, durable until bump). We added the deliberate-toggle-transition trigger because re-enabling AI Assistant after a disable is a deliberate user action that warrants re-acknowledgement of the legal posture each time. The acknowledged version is stored once per deployment (KV Store collection logserv_ai_assistant_acks, _key = the stanza name), not per user, and a Yes and a No both record it. Since build 388 a No on the enable re-ask (the AI Assistant already on) first writes enabled = false - the rest of the draft is not applied - and then records the No, so a failed write leaves the question pending. Since build 389 the dialog closes before the page state changes, and an answer that cannot be recorded also closes the dialog, so its error is seen. The turn-off writes the page’s settings whole, like every Save: a partial write would merge onto readAIConfig(), which falls back to the conf or the defaults when the KV read fails. Since build 390 the page stays busy until a turn-off’s No is recorded, a No’s audit event records the saved provider, and the forwarder dialog also closes before a record or save error is shown. Since build 391 handleForwarderChoice posts the forwarder acknowledgement’s audit event as soon as the answer is recorded (a Yes’s event used to wait for actuallySave’s successful write, which no longer takes an acceptance), and on a re-ask the enablement dialog names saved.provider. Since build 392 AuditWriter.postOneOff reads the local index and the forwarder settings before its first await, so the settings in place when a one-off event is posted decide where it goes, and a failed forward’s record goes to the event’s index; on a re-ask whose save changes the provider, the dialog also gets pendingProviderName.

telemetryConfApi.ts exposes readTcAcknowledgement(stanza) / writeTcAcknowledgement(stanza, choice, version) parameterized by stanza name. The two modal stanzas are constants: STANZA_FORWARDER_TC and STANZA_ENABLE_TC.

The legacy conf-writer path coerces yes/no to '1'/'0'; the KV Store path stores the strings as-is. The audit event preserves the literal string in _raw, so the audit event is the canonical record while the stored acknowledgement is the state marker.

docs.title: Why Primer Rules Beat Other Fixes (TIME-WINDOW REASONING)
docs.text:
One alternative fix was considered before settling on primer rules for the time-window reasoning behavior: surfacing the dispatch window in Tier 2 metadata even for non-_time results, which would let the AI see the window directly without reasoning about it. Higher engineering effort than primer rules; deferred unless rules alone don’t move the needle.

Primer rules were the cheapest test of “is this a primer-rules issue?” and it worked: same prompt, same data, dramatically better self-correction behavior in one turn instead of needing a follow-up prompt to re-rank cumulative-noise findings.

This is the canonical pattern: when the AI has the data but isn’t using it correctly, primer rules are the cheapest first attempt. When the AI doesn’t have the data, metadata expansion is the next step.

docs.title: Splunk Static-Asset Cache Busting
docs.text:
Splunk Web caches the React bundle’s asset URL under a hash that includes the [install] build integer in app.conf. Re-deploying the same build number with new bytes serves stale assets even after Splunkd restart. Always bump the build number for any meaningful code change.

The 3-part SemVer in [id] version is independent and only changes on user-facing version bumps. AppInspect’s pretrained / Splunkbase precert rules require 3-part SemVer, so directory naming uses a 4-part vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.SNAPSHOT form for snapshot-tracking purposes only — the app.conf [id] version stays 3-part.

docs.title: Live UI Refresh on Settings Save
docs.text:
When the admin saves a config change in the General tab that affects what users see (master enabled toggle, mcp_required, power_user_roles, etc.), the React app re-runs loadAIAssistantConfig() immediately and re-applies the new config to the running session. No page reload required.

Implementation: App.tsx accepts an onConfigSaved callback that re-loads config from the storage REST API. The callback is threaded App → AppShell → AIAssistantSettings → GeneralPanel, called after writeAIConfig succeeds. Affected props are recomputed on the next React render and the dependent UI re-renders accordingly (e.g., the AI Assistant button in the header appears / disappears).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This document covers the internal architecture of the SAP LogServ TA’s filtering and deployment automation system. It is intended for developers who need to maintain, extend, or test the TA.

The filtering system provides index-time event filtering via TRANSFORMS-based queue routing. It includes a UI built on UCC (Splunk Universal Configuration Console), custom REST handlers, deployment server automation, and background scripted inputs for daily maintenance and upgrade detection.

docs.title: Architecture Summary
docs.text:
+-------------------------------------------------------+
|  Splunk Web (UCC Configuration UI)                    |
|  Configuration -> Filters + Cloud Provider tabs       |
|  + filter_settings_hook.js (Deploy button, banners)   |
+---------------------------+---------------------------+
                            | Save
                            v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|  splunk_ta_sap_logserv_rh_filter_settings.py (REST Handler) |
|  - Validates patterns                                       |
|  - Saves settings to settings conf                          |
|  - Generates local/transforms.conf + local/props.conf       |
|  - Mirrors to deployment-apps/ (if DS)                      |
|  - Creates server class (if DS, first time)                 |
|  - Reloads confs via REST API                               |
+---------------------------+---------------------------------+
                            |
              +-------------+-------------+
              v                           v
    +------------+          +--------------------+
    | Single     |          | Deployment Server  |
    | Instance   |          |                    |
    | (done)     |          | deployment-apps/   |
    +------------+          | + serverclass.conf |
                            | + Deploy button    |
                            +---------+----------+
                                      | Phone home
                                      v
                            +------------------+
                            | Heavy Forwarders |
                            | (receive TA +    |
                            |  filter configs) |
                            +------------------+

docs.title: Source File Map
docs.text:
All source files live under the UCC package directory:

sap_logserv_package/splunk_ta_sap_logserv/
├── globalConfig.json                          # UCC UI definition (Filters + Cloud Provider tabs)
├── additional_packaging.py                    # UCC post-build patcher (see note below)
├── run_appinspect.sh                          # Dev tool — MUST stay outside package/ (an
│                                              #   executable in package/ trips check_for_bin_files)
└── package/
    ├── app.manifest                                # TA version and metadata
    ├── bin/
    │   ├── splunk_ta_sap_logserv_filter_utils.py        # Core library
    │   ├── splunk_ta_sap_logserv_rh_filter_settings.py  # REST handler: Filters + Cloud Provider tabs
    │   ├── splunk_ta_sap_logserv_rh_deployment_push.py  # REST handler: Deploy button
    │   ├── logserv_filter_time_refresh.py               # Daily epoch cutoff refresh
    │   └── logserv_filter_upgrade_check.py              # Upgrade coverage check
    ├── default/
    │   ├── transforms.conf    # Sourcetype routing + @logserv_filter annotations
    │   ├── props.conf         # Sourcetype configs, TRANSFORMS chains
    │   ├── inputs.conf        # Scripted input schedules
    │   ├── macros.conf        # Index name redirect macro
    │   ├── indexes.conf       # Index definitions (folded in from the retired Index App)
    │   └── data/ui/nav/default.xml   # Nav (Configuration + search only)
    ├── metadata/
    │   └── default.meta       # Default permissions and export settings
    ├── static/                # App icons (appIcon*.png)
    ├── LICENSES/              # Absorbed-add-on license texts
    └── appserver/static/js/build/custom/
        ├── filter_settings_hook.js   # UCC hook (DS detection, Deploy button)
        └── cloud_provider_hook.js    # UCC hook (Cloud Provider tab)

additional_packaging.py is load-bearing for AppInspect posture

The post-build patcher performs several jobs after ucc-gen runs: patching every [admin_external:*] restmap stanza (handlertype, python.version, python.required = 3.13, passSystemAuth = true), appending the deployment_push restmap + web.conf expose stanzas, patching inputs.conf [script://...] stanzas with python.required = 3.13, restoring sc_subadmin to the write ACL in the UCC-generated metadata/default.meta, and swapping the generated settings handler import to FilterSettingsHandler. Several of these are AppInspect Cloud gating fixes — deleting or truncating the file silently regresses AppInspect posture and locks out sc_subadmin admins.

docs.title: Core Library
docs.text:
splunk_ta_sap_logserv_filter_utils.py

This is the central module. All other components import from it.

docs.title: Key Functions
docs.text: Function Purpose get_app_path() Determines the app installation path (checks SPLUNK_HOME, falls back to relative path) discover_supported_types(app_path) Scans default/transforms.conf for @logserv_filter annotations find_uncovered_types(supported, patterns) Compares supported types against user include patterns parse_comma_patterns(string) Splits a folder-pattern field (Include / Exclude Filters) into a list; empty entries are dropped parse_source_patterns(value) Splits a source field (Include / Exclude Sources) into its entries; only spaces around an entry are stripped, and empty entries are kept so that validation rejects a doubled or trailing comma validate_patterns(patterns, field_name) Validates folder-pattern syntax (dir/subdir format, valid characters) validate_single_pattern(pattern) Validates one folder pattern against rules validate_source_entry(entry) / validate_source_patterns(patterns, field_name) Validate source entries against the grammar in Validation Layers; the message names the field and the entry validate_source_field(value, field_name) Validates a whole source field value as submitted or stored: its length, then every entry filter_pattern_fragment(pattern) The hand-written translator f(p): one folder segment or source pattern to the REGEX fragment of a JSON value; raises on any character it does not know filter_lookahead(key, fragment) One condition LA(key, frag) for clz_dir, clz_subdir or source is_pass_all_include(include_patterns) Whether Include Filters keeps every event (no include gate) fnmatch_patterns_to_combined_regex(patterns) Compatibility helper kept for existing importers: one REGEX in the generator’s shape for a folder list, without chunking epoch_cutoff_from_days(days_in_past) Computes the epoch timestamp for midnight N days ago (UTC) generate_epoch_less_than_regex(cutoff_epoch) Generates a digit-by-digit regex matching epoch values less than the cutoff generate_transforms_stanzas(include, exclude, days, include_sources=None, exclude_sources=None) Generates the filter transform stanzas; re-validates every entry and raises on an invalid one generate_props_filter_lines(include, exclude, days, enabled, include_sources=None, exclude_sources=None) Generates the TRANSFORMS-00-filter line naming exactly the stanzas generate_transforms_stanzas emits, in chain order write_local_conf(app_path, conf_name, content) Writes between marker comments in local conf files write_local_conf_section(app_path, conf_name, content, marker_start, marker_end) Generalised marker-block writer — lets two independent marker blocks (filter + cloud provider) coexist in one local conf update_local_stanza(app_path, conf_name, stanza, kv) Direct filesystem stanza write — the RestError[403] fallback used when the caller lacks admin_all_objects get_ta_version(app_path) Reads version from default/app.conf (falls back to app.manifest if not present) get_server_roles(session_key) Queries /services/server/info for roles is_deployment_server(session_key) Two-step DS detection (roles + client probe) get_deployment_apps_path() Returns the etc/deployment-apps/ path for the TA ensure_deployment_app_synced(app_path) Full app copy/upgrade to deployment-apps/ mirror_to_deployment_apps(app_path) Copies local/transforms.conf and local/props.conf ensure_serverclass(session_key) Creates server class + app mapping via REST + file

docs.title: Constants
docs.text: Constant Value Purpose APP_NAME splunk_ta_sap_logserv App directory name SERVERCLASS_NAME SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders Auto-created server class name SETTINGS_CONF splunk_ta_sap_logserv_settings UCC settings conf file FILTER_STANZA filter_settings Stanza name in settings conf SYSTEM_MESSAGE_NAME logserv_filter_upgrade_warning System message banner name for upgrade warnings ANNOTATION_PATTERN Compiled regex Matches @logserv_filter: annotation comment lines VALID_SEGMENT_PATTERN Compiled regex Validates characters in dir/subdir pattern segments FILTER_REGEX_SKIP Regex text (SKIP in Filter Regex Generation) Where every generated filter REGEX starts: the line start, or just past the _raw value FILTER_REGEX_GAP Regex text (the gap inside LA in Filter Regex Generation) What a lookahead may cross before its key: anything on the line except a "_raw" key FILTER_LOOKAHEAD 100000 LOOKAHEAD of every generated filter stanza (= TRUNCATE in default/props.conf) FILTER_REGEX_MAX_CHARS 8000 A list whose REGEX would pass this many characters is split into numbered stanzas SOURCE_PATTERN_MAX_LEN / SOURCE_FIELD_MAX_LEN 512 / 4096 Longest source pattern / longest source field value FILTER_MARKER_START / FILTER_MARKER_END Marker comments Delimit generated filter content in local conf files CLOUD_PROVIDER_MARKER_START / CLOUD_PROVIDER_MARKER_END Marker comments Delimit the generated [logserv_set_cloud_provider] block — separate from the filter block so the daily time-refresh preserves it

docs.title: Configuration REST Handler (Filters + Cloud Provider tabs)
docs.text:
splunk_ta_sap_logserv_rh_filter_settings.py

UCC REST handler (extends AdminExternalHandler) registered in globalConfig.json. UCC generates ONE MultipleModel settings endpoint shared by all Configuration tabs, so this single handler class serves both the Filters and the Cloud Provider tab — it dispatches on the payload (if 'cloud_provider' in self.callerArgs.data), validating against VALID_CLOUD_PROVIDERS and writing/clearing the [logserv_set_cloud_provider] override inside its own ### BEGIN/END LOGSERV CLOUD_PROVIDER CONFIG ### marker block. For a Filters save it handles the Save action:

  1. Validates patterns server-side (blocks save on failure via admin.ArgValidationException): include_sources and exclude_sources on every save, then every posted value on every save for conf safety (_validate_posted_values(): no control character, tab included, and no trailing backslash), the folder patterns and Days in the Past when filtering is enabled — see Validation Layers
  2. Saves settings to splunk_ta_sap_logserv_settings.conf (default UCC behavior — the happy path). Falls back to a direct filesystem write when the UCC REST write raises RestError[403] (“This operation is forbidden”): splunkd gates /configs/conf-* writes on admin_all_objects independently of the object metadata ACL, so Splunk Cloud sc_subadmin and hardened on-prem admin roles fail the REST path. update_local_stanza() writes the stanza to local/<settings>.conf directly, bypassing that gate (passSystemAuth is NOT honoured for UCC [admin_external:*] handlers)
  3. Generates local/transforms.conf and local/props.conf with filter stanzas, from all five filter fields (include_filters, exclude_filters, include_sources, exclude_sources, days_in_past) as saved: _effective_filter_settings() takes each field the request posts (an emptied field is '', as splunktaucclib stores it), and for a field a partial REST/CLI save leaves out the stored value (one GET of configs/conf-splunk_ta_sap_logserv_settings/filter_settings, only when a field is missing; on a read failure the old defaults, with a WARNING). Step 1 dry-runs the generators on these values when filtering is enabled, so a value they would refuse is refused before anything is saved
  4. Syncs and mirrors to deployment-apps if on a DS (full app copy/upgrade + filter configs)
  5. Creates server class if on a DS (first time only)
  6. Reloads confs via REST API (/configs/conf-transforms/_reload, /configs/conf-props/_reload)
  7. Checks for uncovered types and manages system message banner

docs.title: Deploy Button REST Handler
docs.text:
splunk_ta_sap_logserv_rh_deployment_push.py

Persistent REST handler (PersistentServerConnectionApplication) registered in restmap.conf. Provides two endpoints:

  • GET /services/splunk_ta_sap_logserv/deployment_push — Returns is_deployment_server boolean and server class status (used by the JS hook to render the UI)
  • POST — Triggers deployment reload via /services/deployment/server/config/_reload

Note

Persistent handlers do NOT get import_declare_test. They require explicit sys.path setup for the app’s bin/ and lib/ directories at the top of the file.

Note

Custom persistent endpoints require an [expose:] stanza in web.conf to be accessible through the Splunk Web proxy (port 8000). This is handled by additional_packaging.py during the UCC build.

docs.title: UCC Hook
docs.text:
filter_settings_hook.js

JavaScript hook loaded by UCC on the Filters tab. Lifecycle methods:

  • onCreate / onRender / onEditLoad — Calls checkDeploymentServer() to GET the deployment push endpoint. If DS detected, injects the deploy banner, server class guidance notices, and Deploy button into the DOM
  • onSaveSuccess — Triggers window.location.reload() after 500ms to reflect server-side changes

docs.title: Daily Time Refresh
docs.text:
logserv_filter_time_refresh.py

Scripted input (runs every 86400 seconds / once per day):

  1. Reads filter settings from the settings conf via REST — all six keys: filter_enabled, include_filters, exclude_filters, include_sources, exclude_sources, days_in_past
  2. Regenerates local/transforms.conf and local/props.conf with updated epoch cutoff regex
  3. Mirrors to deployment-apps if on a DS
  4. Reloads the SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders server class if on a DS, in the namespace of the app that holds it (see below), so the Heavy Forwarders fetch the new cutoff on their next phone-home
  5. Reloads confs

It does steps 2–5 only while filtering is enabled and days_in_past is above 0; otherwise it logs why and exits.

Where the scoped reload is sent. A server-class reload (deployment/server/serverclasses/<name>/reload) has to be sent in the namespace of the app whose serverclass.conf holds the class. ensure_serverclass() creates the class through /services/... as the admin who saves the filters, so it lands in that admin’s default app — search on the reference deployment server, where its ACL reads app = search, owner = nobody, sharing = app. Earlier builds POSTed /services/deployment/server/serverclasses/SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders/reload, which resolves in the default app of splunk-system-user (the input’s passAuth user); whether that found the class was never established. The refresh now resolves the namespace instead:

  1. GET /servicesNS/-/-/deployment/server/serverclasses/SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders?output_mode=json (read-only) and take entry[0].acl.app; the value is used only if it is a plain app name — it matches [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+ and is not dots only — because it becomes part of a URL path
  2. POST /servicesNS/nobody/<app>/deployment/server/serverclasses/SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders/reload
  3. On any failure — no owning app, a refused or failed POST — fall back to /servicesNS/nobody/search/..., then to /services/...; a path already tried is not tried again, and the first HTTP 200 or 201 ends the sequence

It logs at INFO which path reloaded the class, or a WARNING that lists every path tried and its result when none did. No reload failure raises out of main(), and the conf reload of step 5 runs either way. A failed reload only delays the forwarders: they keep the previous cutoff until the next Deploy to Forwarders, and a stale cutoff is less restrictive — older events pass — never more.

A working reload restarts the forwarders once a day. The cutoff text changes every UTC day, so each run gives the forwarders a changed app, and ensure_serverclass() maps the Data TA with restartSplunkd = true — each Heavy Forwarder in the class restarts to apply it. The refresh runs every 86,400 seconds counted from the deployment server’s last start, so that restart is not tied to a maintenance window. Only a deployment server with filtering enabled and days_in_past above 0 does this.

It must read every filter field. The refresh rewrites the whole FILTER marker block, so a field it does not read and pass to the generators disappears from the generated rules within a day — and on a DS the stripped block is mirrored and pushed to the Heavy Forwarders by the scoped reload. Any new filter field must be threaded through this script as well as the REST handler.
